rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes tensile or creep tests on a single-phase, fine-grained alloy with matched grain size to pure tungsten, whereas the paper used arc-melted, as-cast material with a two-phase dendritic microstructure and tested via compression, indentation plastometry, and scratch testing without matching grain sizes. This represents a different processing route and test method, making it a different kind of study.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature testing at 800–1000 °C under controlled strain rates mimicking plasma-facing-component service, while the paper conducted room-temperature compression, indentation plastometry from room temperature to 500 °C, and room-temperature scratch testing. These are different temperature regimes and loading modes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes severe lattice distortion creating a heterogeneous energy landscape that impedes abrupt dislocation motion, promoting distributed dislocation activation and strain hardening. rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher plastic strain, increased strain-hardening rate, and higher fracture toughness under high-temperature loading. The paper predicts and finds higher strength, greater plastic strain, lower brittle-to-ductile transition temperature, less scratch-induced cracking, and higher fracture toughness, but at lower temperatures (up to 500 °C) and under different loading modes.
